_comment: Deterministic deny rules for the PreToolUse safety hook. This gates ONLY what the driver AUTO-EXECUTES via Bash; it never limits exploitation code the driver authors for the operator to run (author-and-handoff). Gate is on EFFECTS, not methods: scope/domain and technique/payload are intentionally NOT restricted - only never-justified, irreversible / harm-as-purpose effect categories are blocked (destruction, 拖库/dump, DoS, money, harm-as-goal payloads). Each rule blocks a Bash command when its regex matches (case-insensitive, against the raw command string). Edit/extend freely; the hook falls back to built-in defaults if this file is missing or invalid.

rules.reason: recursive/forced deletion of a CATASTROPHIC target (root / home / system dir / drive root / bare * . ..); repo-relative deletes fall through to the ask/allow flow

recursive/forced rm of a DATA directory (/data, /backup(s), /var/lib, /var/www, /home/<user>/<deep>) -- irreversible data loss the catastrophic-path rule above misses (it only matches one level deep on listed system dirs). Closes the F5 gap from the 2026-06-15 hook review.

destructive rm -rf SHIPPED TO A TARGET as a payload (a quoted rm -rf inside a request, alongside a URL) -- destroying target data is never a proof step. Narrowed from the old any-rm-co-located-with-any-URL form (which false-fired on a STANDALONE local scratch rm that merely shared a line with a probe URL); the rm -rf must now appear INSIDE a quoted string (i.e. injected as data). Catastrophic local rm is still covered by the root/system-path rule above; benign repo-relative rm falls through to ask/allow.
raw write to a disk device (dd of=/dev/...)
ransomware-style backup/shadow-copy destruction (vssadmin/wbadmin/wmic delete shadows) -- harm-as-purpose, never auto

secure-wipe / overwrite destruction (shred/sdelete/cipher /w/wipefs/blkdiscard, and the scrub disk-wipe tool when invoked on a device/with flags) -- irreversible, never auto. Narrowed scrub from bare \bscrub\b (which false-fired on the English word 'scrub' and on read-only zpool/btrfs scrub) to scrub with a flag or /dev/ target

host shutdown/reboot/halt/poweroff at COMMAND POSITION (line start, newline, after ;/&&/||, optional sudo), incl. absolute-path (/sbin/shutdown) and systemctl forms (systemctl poweroff/reboot/halt). Narrowed from bare \b(shutdown|…)\b which false-fired on the word as DATA: method calls (srv.shutdown(), logging.shutdown()), grep/echo args (grep 'shutdown|reboot', echo shutdown), URL params (?x=1&shutdown=now). Single | and single & are NOT separators (you never pipe-into or URL-param a real shutdown). Accepted gaps (recoverable effect, evasion-shaped): bash -c "shutdown", cmd & shutdown.
runlevel halt/reboot via init/telinit (init 0 = halt, init 6 = reboot) at command position; requires the literal runlevel digit so it does not fire on 'git init' / npm init / __init__

Windows host shutdown/restart (Stop-Computer / Restart-Computer) at COMMAND POSITION (line start, newline, after ;/&&/||) -- native PowerShell host power control; recoverable but disruptive, never auto. Command-position-anchored (like the shutdown rule) so the cmdlet name as DATA (echo/grep/docs) does not false-fire. Accepted gaps (recoverable + evasion-shaped, symmetric to the shutdown rule): scriptblock / Invoke-Command (&{Restart-Computer}, Invoke-Command -ScriptBlock {...}), single-pipe (X | Restart-Computer -- note PS does accept pipeline input here), call-operator (& Restart-Computer), single-& background.
unscoped row deletion (DELETE FROM without WHERE)

rules._comment_permission_soft: Permission/ownership/role/ACL/privilege changes (chmod/chown/setfacl/set-role/cloud IAM/k8s RBAC) are SOFT rules now — operator-gated in src-safety-boundary, NOT machine-blocked. They are reversible (non-destructive), so they are not denied here.

rules.reason: state-changing request to a money/transfer endpoint

rules._comment_proof_line: Active proof tools (sqlmap/nuclei/payloads) are ALLOWED for proof-only verification; these rules block ONLY the switches that cross the proof line into dumping data, writing files, or spawning shells.
rules.reason: sqlmap data-dump / file-write / OS-shell switch crosses the proof line (proof of injection is allowed; extracting business data or shells is not)
nuclei dos/intrusive/fuzz templates exceed proof-only verification
sqlmap high risk/level expands payloads beyond proof-only verification
